system.name: Melange stance and tone measurement (press and social text)
system.description: Turns member press releases, tweets and other posts into signed CU stance and tone. Covers the Political DEBATE NLI stance reader, Lexicoder tone, two-hop stance x valence composition, bill-sign handling, CFPB axis isolation, human-label overlay, the media blend with recency decay, ACU speaker mode, stance dynamics and frame alignment. It includes the legacy Draft Systems R regex scorer (Stage 5).

components.name: Fine-tuned Political DEBATE NLI stance reader
components.computes: Per-release (and per-tweet) stance toward credit-union interests: support, oppose or neutral (sign -1/0/+1).
components.method: mlburnham/Political_DEBATE_base_v1.0 fine-tuned on cu_stance_label_set.csv (552 rows; seed 42; 3 epochs). A Claude rater pre-labelled and human labels override. CPU, about 0.3 s per document. Reported results: 87.2% vs Claude (distillation); about 85% / kappa 0.76 on a member-grouped human-gold test; ft accuracy 0.839 / kappa 0.742 held out; 0.796 on the 760-row gold frame; 0.571 on the adversarial goldeval frame. It is one of five readers in the stacked press stack and the fallback reader in build_media_blend.
assumptions: Policy stance toward CUs is recoverable from text by NLI entailment
DEBATE neutral means the text is not about the bill, not a missed stance
The held-out test sets (87 or 156 rows) are representative
empirical_questions: Does a fine-tuned NLI stance model outperform supervised TF-IDF/SVM on a member-grouped held-out set of this size (83.9% LinearSVC vs 0.757 transformer reported)?
How much of the accuracy is agreement with the LLM pre-labeller rather than with humans?
Does accuracy drop on adversarial and sign-flip targets (CFPB, interchange) as the 0.571 goldeval figure suggests?
components.heading: Fine-tuned Political DEBATE NLI stance reader

components.name: Supervised and stacked stance readers
components.computes: Stacked stance label per tweet or press item from classical and API readers.
components.method: Best classical model: LinearSVC on word+char TF-IDF, 83.9% / macro-F1 0.816 on untouched test (n=87). Khan-style multi-view augmentation was tested and hurt classical models. Supervised tweet stance reached 0.737 CV on 399 golds. Stanceformer is planned, not built.
assumptions: Target-specific labels are needed; sentiment is not stance
The 456/87/217 split is never reshuffled; CV of about 0.90 is inflated and not quoted
empirical_questions: Does target-aware attention (Stanceformer) improve the neutral class over a TF-IDF SVM on this corpus?
Does paired-input augmentation help transformer readers when it hurts classical readers?
components.heading: Supervised and stacked stance readers

components.name: Lexicoder LSD2015 tone intensity
components.computes: Per-release tone intensity = |net| / words from LSD2015 positive, negative and negated counts.
components.method: stringi regex implementation that matches quanteda data_dictionary_LSD2015 counts; negation phrases are stripped first; 9.6 ms per document.
assumptions: Dictionary counts measure how heated a release is (intensity, not direction)
empirical_questions: Does LSD intensity on congressional press releases correlate with human-coded intensity?
Does multiplying stance sign by tone intensity improve prediction of behaviour over stance sign alone?
components.heading: Lexicoder LSD2015 tone intensity

components.name: press_value aggregate and human-label overlay
components.computes: press_value = stance_sign x LSD intensity per member x category. Human labels overwrite model stance where valid; 497 of 552 labels overlap the corpus.
components.method: run_stage5.R block 3c is placed after the bill override and the Kennedy fix. Overlaid rows are excluded from model-accuracy measurement.
assumptions: Human labels are authoritative
Overlay rows cannot be used to measure DEBATE accuracy
empirical_questions: How much of the member-level press score is driven by human-overlaid rows versus model rows?
components.heading: press_value aggregate and human-label overlay

components.name: Two-hop stance x valence decomposition with curated registry
components.method: Measured on 400 tweet golds: stance hop 0.915, valence hop 0.689 (the bottleneck). Composing model stance with oracle valence gives 0.872. Valence registry cu_valence_registry.json v2 (11 derived plus 14 seed entries) is derived from Paul's gold judgments; with 5-fold CV the composition reaches 0.782 accuracy / 0.754 F1 vs a flat baseline of 0.677. Auto-registry variants all fell below the flat baseline.
assumptions: Each target has a stable CU valence the owner can judge
Per-target valence is not keyword-automatable (238 distinct targets in 400 tweets)
empirical_questions: Does an explicit two-stage (target stance, then target valence) label schema beat end-to-end CU-alignment labels on held-out data, as TSE-style decoupling predicts?
How stable is a target's CU valence across Congresses?
Does registry coverage, rather than stance accuracy, explain most residual error?
components.heading: Two-hop stance x valence decomposition with curated registry

components.name: Bill-sign valence (direction table, prose matcher; override rejected)
components.computes: Stance sign from a tracked bill's known CU direction when a release names the bill.
components.method: cfpb_bill_directions.csv (Reduce +1 / Expand -1) plus the BILLS table in cu_press_release_scraper.R. The named-bill matcher had 93% precision on 187 releases but went 0 good / 3 bad as a blanket override. The DEBATE bill-sign override (12-member anti-CU prior list) dropped held-out accuracy from 0.839 / kappa 0.742 to 0.770 / 0.630 and was disabled 2026-06-30. The naive directional-verb lexicon (after Park, Lee & Cho 2025) gave 3 good / 43 bad sign changes and was rejected. The narrow Kennedy per-release fix is kept.
assumptions: REFUTED: DEBATE neutral means a missed bill stance
REFUTED: directional verb counts over whole text determine valence
Member priors (anti-bank consumer advocates) need a member-level prior, not a lexicon
empirical_questions: Would an aboutness or prominence guard (the bill is the main topic) make a bill-sign override net-positive on held-out gold?
Does a direction-aware lexicon work when restricted to the sentence that names the bill?
components.heading: Bill-sign valence (direction table, prose matcher; override rejected)

components.name: CFPB axis isolation (registry families plus binding policy_force)
components.computes: CFPB stance split into restraint (+1), expansion (-1), institution (0) and general (0) families.
components.method: policy_force is a binding post-meta override in both stacks, and the CATKW router was tightened. CFPB-negative tiers went D 123 -> 98, R 7 -> 0; no-evidence 174 -> 263.
assumptions: CFPB restraint vs expansion is separable by registry families
CFPB-negative tiers were confounded by party (123 D vs 7 R)
empirical_questions: After isolation, is the CFPB-negative tier still predicted by party once bill-level CFPB votes are controlled?
code_refs: fec/stance registry and CATKW router (exact file not named)
components.heading: CFPB axis isolation (registry families plus binding policy_force)

components.name: Media blend (press + social) with recency decay
components.computes: raw cell = (1-0.5f) press/p80 + 0.5f social/p80, with f = min(1, nz/15) shrinkage for thin categories.
components.method: Per post: sign x clip(margin, .25, 1.5) x (0.5 if retweet) x 0.5^(age/HL) / n_categories. Half-life is 2.0 years for press and 0.5 years for social. The press-side recency_weight in the R scraper also uses a 2-year half-life with a 2022-01-01 floor. 20 categories via CATKW regex; CROSSPOST_DEDUP is off by default.
assumptions: Stance salience decays exponentially at the stated half-lives
Social posts carry stance comparable to press after p80 scaling
Thin categories (under 15 members with signal) are unreliable
empirical_questions: What half-life best predicts subsequent votes from past statements?
Do social posts add predictive validity over press releases given that many are ghost-written?
Is shrinkage at nz/15 well calibrated?
components.heading: Media blend (press + social) with recency decay

components.name: Legacy CU press regex stance and graded tone scorer
components.computes: Per release: CU stance via a regex ladder (default support), graded tone via TONE_LEXICON, and member lean, stance and negativity aggregates.
components.method: Ladder: oppose > support cues > neutral bill cues > default support. GRADED_CUTS c(1,2,3.5,5.5,8). Polarity (Wp-Wn)/(Wp+Wn) per Rice & Zorn. Over-flagging recorded: 21 of 32 neutrals were wrongly scored. Superseded for stance on 2026-06-21 and still computed as a comparison column.
assumptions: CU-mention sentences carry the release's CU stance
Default stance is support
empirical_questions: How biased is a default-support regex relative to human gold, by party?
components.heading: Legacy CU press regex stance and graded tone scorer

components.name: ACU speaker mode (planned)
components.computes: Treats ACU-authored press (816 rows, 243 members) as ACU-to-member friend or foe labels.
components.method: The NLI hypothesis is branched by speaker_source; keyword extraction was rejected. Validation gate: held-out accuracy >= 0.851, and Marshall/Hawley ACU rows must net negative. Planned 2026-07-01 and blocked on labels.
assumptions: ACU endorsing a member means pro-CU; ACU criticising a member means anti-CU
empirical_questions: Do advocacy-group statements about a member predict that member's subsequent CU votes better than the member's own statements?
components.heading: ACU speaker mode (planned)

components.name: Stance dynamics and neighbour imputation
components.computes: Quarterly (91-day) stance trajectories in seven classes, plus imputation proposals for missing stances from network neighbours.
components.method: Static band = median + MAD over observed-to-observed transitions (floor .05). Imputation needs at least 5 neighbours and |estimate| >= 0.75; 307 proposals; masking validation gives 77% sign agreement. Proposals only; the matrix is not changed. Co-movement was null on the cosponsor and HCoI layers.
assumptions: Stance is locally similar among network neighbours (co-movement test was null)
empirical_questions: Does neighbour-based stance imputation beat a party-only baseline on masked members?
Do stance changes propagate along cosponsor ties over quarters?
components.heading: Stance dynamics and neighbour imputation

components.name: Frame alignment (cross-member duplication rate)
components.computes: Per-category share of near-duplicate text across members, plus party framing chi-square.
components.method: 3-gram shingle Jaccard >= 0.5. Reported duplication: CU Tax 65%, General CU 60%, Defense 12%. It feeds salience intensity (0.5 + alignment).
assumptions: High shingle overlap indicates coordinated messaging
empirical_questions: Does coordinated (duplicated) messaging predict collective cosponsorship on the same bill?
components.heading: Frame alignment (cross-member duplication rate)

positions.paul_position: Paul endorses LLM- and transformer-based position extraction (Kim's GPT-4 labels at 96.9% vs human; Birkenmaier's finding that GPT-4o beats SVM and XLM-R). He notes a weakness: disentangling ambiguous statements.
Paul's highlights call bag-of-words SVM baselines outdated next to LLMs. Peng's stacking reduces long-distance dependency but does not remove it. Paul plans to re-read Peng.
No annotation. Paul highlighted Merkley & Stecula's use of Lexicoder with custom dictionaries to measure party cues.
Paul treats sentiment-scored press as an augmentation to lobbying-pathway models. His notes do not discuss the human-label overlay.

Paul asked how agreement between actors is quantified when both hold negative sentiment toward a third member. The stance-times-valence registry is the system's answer, which his notes do not yet record.
Kim's bill positions (Support, Oppose, Engage) are the model for per-bill signing. Paul's critique is that the method is reactive and does not show inter-industry conflict.

Paul calls for temporal weighting to capture shifting relationships. His sources give decay timescales: Sotoudeh's 6-month half-life, and Kim's effects that fade within 2 to 3 years. The system's 2.0-year press and 0.5-year social half-lives were not drawn from his notes.
No annotated literature; Rice & Zorn is on disk but unannotated.

Paul's highlights stress that endorsements from well-connected groups are strong cues, and that the identity of the source shapes receptiveness. Both support treating ACU-authored statements as a separate signal.
Paul wants temporal dynamics and change-likelihood modeling. His notes predate the null co-movement result.
Joo's frame alignment through duplicate rates (highlighted) is the template. Paul's margin note on Joo ('Monitoring tool?') concerns Dietrich's video-based aisle crossing.

evidence.title: D-NOMINATE After 10 Years: A Comparative Update to Congress: A Political Economic History of Roll Call Voting
evidence.claim: Party overlap is under 1.5 percent in both chambers for the past 5 Congresses (p.15). The paper states, citing McCarty, Poole and Rosenthal (1999) rather than presenting evidence, that party per se does not account for much roll-call voting over and above the spatial model (p.17).
evidence.system_side: Brain records CFPB-negative tiers as a confirmed party proxy (D 123 vs R 7), and after axis isolation D 98 vs R 0. dw_control.py provides a dim1 and extremity loader for psychometric residualization; within fec it is imported only by hearing_antagonism_build.py, not by any stance code. bluesky_stance_stack.py:46 defines POLICY_KEYS, the CFPB policy_force axis.
evidence.transfer: With near-zero overlap, dim1 and party are nearly collinear; the informative test is within-party. A pooled coefficient carries the UNSTRATIFIED label.

evidence.title: Measuring Interest Group Positions on Legislation: An AI-Driven Analysis of Lobbying Reports
evidence.claim: The released dataset gives measured group positions on named S./H.R. bills for the 111th-117th Congresses (2009-2022). It is on Dataverse at doi:10.7910/DVN/D0QWM2.
evidence.system_side: A bill's CU direction comes from a 60-row hand table, cfpb_bill_directions.csv (Direction 1 = Reduce, -1 = Expand; 5 Expand rows).
evidence.transfer: Useful as an external audit of the hand-set direction table, but only for 111th-117th Congress bills that CU trade associations named in LD-2 lines. 118th and 119th Congress bills would need the Haiku lane. Use it to adjudicate the table, never to overwrite it.

evidence.title: Measuring Interest Group Positions on Legislation: An AI-Driven Analysis of Lobbying Reports
evidence.claim: GPT-4 zero-shot labelling at temperature 0 reaches 96.93% accuracy on 391 coder-agreed lobbying lines. The lines pass a keyword filter for position terms first (e.g. endorse, defeat, advocate, watch).
evidence.system_side: stage5_debate.py runs Political DEBATE zero-shot NLI to score each press release's stance toward credit unions (support, oppose and neutral hypotheses). Audit documents (not the code) report the fine-tuned reader at 0.839 accuracy on a held-out human-gold test (n=87) and 0.571 on the adversarial frame.
evidence.transfer: Does not transfer. Kim's text is pre-filtered to explicit position terms about a named bill, and the validation set excludes coder disagreements. Press stance toward CUs needs a target-valence step that Kim's task lacks. The 96.9% is not a benchmark for this reader.

evidence.title: Twitter as Data
evidence.claim: Every US Senator and 430 House members had official Twitter accounts (2016). Tweet author metadata reflects when the API request was made, not when the tweet was created.
evidence.system_side: The media blend gives social posts half the weight of each member-category cell, with SOCIAL_W 0.5, a 0.5-year half-life (decay 0.5^(age/HL)) and nz/15 shrinkage where social signal is thin. Members are attributed through a handle registry; unverified Bluesky handles are flagged and kept out of the member rollup.
evidence.transfer: The coverage figure supports the assumption that almost all members have a social channel, but it counts Twitter accounts in 2016. It does not count the 119th Congress, it does not cover the platform mix the system reads (X, Facebook, Truth Social, Bluesky), and it says nothing about how many posts each member makes on CU topics. The metadata-timing caveat applies to handle-to-member mapping done at collection time. It does not apply to decay, which uses the post date. The paper offers nothing on ghost-writing, on the half-life, or on whether social posts add predictive validity over press releases.

evidence.title: Image as Data: Automated Content Analysis for Visual Presentations of Political Actors and Events
evidence.claim: Framing = share of duplicate images within each event-label; two images are duplicates when the normalized distance between their 1,000-dim last fully connected layer vectors is below .2. Table 3: Venezuela state violence .308 vs Hong Kong contains-child .003 (paper: almost 103 times). The paper frames this as measuring which frames protesters choose to share.
evidence.system_side: Ports the duplication rate to press titles: an item counts as aligned if another member's title in the same category has 3-word-shingle Jaccard >= 0.5. SRC is the full cu_press_stance_tone.csv (2,388 rows) with no domain filter. 816 rows are americascreditunions.org articles; they carry 816 distinct URLs but only 349 distinct titles, with up to 19 members on one title, so one ACU headline attributed to many members scores as cross-member duplication. Recompute (reproduced on a second path with identical numbers; window = whole CSV, file dated 2026-06-30): General Credit Union 60.2% of 442 items -> 5.2% of 116 own-domain (*.senate.gov/*.house.gov) items; Credit Union Tax Status 64.7% of 190 -> 38.1% of 42; Defense 12.2% of 41 -> 13.9% of 36; ACU-only rows 79.8% of 326 (General) and 72.3% of 148 (Tax).
evidence.transfer: Carries over only when the duplicated unit was chosen by the actor being scored, as Joo's sharers chose their images; here that means own-domain releases. Third-party ACU syndication measures the author's reach, not member coordination. Joo's frame labels come from a trained classifier; here they are press categories, and short titles under 3-gram Jaccard >= 0.5 are not comparable to a CNN-feature distance threshold.

evidence.title: Image as Data: Automated Content Analysis for Visual Presentations of Political Actors and Events
evidence.claim: The .2 duplicate threshold was chosen from inspecting the distance histogram, with no sensitivity analysis reported. The authors call the results provisional and suggest other operationalizations such as number of tweets containing a label instead of percentage, and expanding the frames considered.
evidence.system_side: The docstring calls Jaccard >= 0.5 the analog of Joo's .2 distance and inherits the same untested choice. There is no threshold sweep; the only audit check is that alignment rates fall in [0,1]. Echo clusters use the same 0.5 cut with a minimum group of 3 items.
evidence.transfer: Applies directly. Before any alignment figure is quoted, sweep the threshold (e.g. 0.3-0.7) on own-domain rows. The paper supplies no threshold validation the system could borrow.

evidence.title: Image as Data: Automated Content Analysis for Visual Presentations of Political Actors and Events
evidence.claim: Chi-squared tests of label against party are run separately on male and female images because the two parties have different gender ratios. Labels are sorted by chi-square with per-label significance stars; no multiple-comparison correction is described across the 1,730 unique labels.
evidence.system_side: The party-framing block computes chi-squared of press category and title terms against party (D vs R), pooled across chamber and source domain, with no strata and no correction. The pooled input is 1,231 Senate and 1,157 House rows, 816 (34%) of them ACU-authored. The brain note quotes 'D to CU-Bank Dynamics (chi-square = 128)' with no stratum or window.
evidence.transfer: Joo's design stratifies on a known compositional fault line. Here the fault lines are chamber and author domain. Until stratified, quote the chi-square figures as UNSTRATIFIED descriptive term lists, not party-framing findings.

evidence.title: Measuring Politicians' Public Personality Traits Using Computational Text Analysis: A Multimethod Feasibility Study for Agency and Communion
evidence.claim: On the paper's personality-cue task, few-shot LLM prompting (0.77) beats fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa (0.70, strong balanced), which only slightly beats a bag-of-words SVM (0.63 strong balanced; 0.55 to 0.63 across variants).
evidence.system_side: train_stance_domain.py --tune builds a word plus char_wb TF-IDF union with a LinearSVC C grid chosen by CV on train only (lines 74-92). The brain reports the production SVM (word plus char, C=2.0) at 83.9 percent accuracy and 0.816 macro-F1 on the untouched n=87 test, and a transformer at 0.757. These brain figures were not rerun.
evidence.transfer: Different task (CU press and social stance, not German agency and communion cues) and a different baseline: the paper's SVM is word-only with no C tuning. The system's ranking comes from its own held-out test, so this paper cannot rank the system's readers. The code's transformer defaults to distilroberta, not XLM-RoBERTa.

evidence.title: Similarity-based link prediction in social networks using latent relationships between the users
evidence.claim: Many existing edges join nodes with no common neighbour: 53.7% in YST, falling to 3.1% in UAL. Correlation of second-order neighbourhood vectors still separates test from non-existing edges for such pairs, and DICN is best in 5 of 9 networks there.
evidence.system_side: The silent-member imputation proposal averages stance-tier scores over direct cosponsor-graph neighbours only. It needs at least SD_MINNB = 5 informative neighbours and |estimate| >= SD_CONF = 0.75. Members below that get no proposal. The masking check counts sign agreement only on confident estimates.
evidence.transfer: The paper predicts edges, not node attributes, so at most it supports a second-order similarity weight for choosing which neighbours to average. Any second-order variant is a proposal that must beat a party-only baseline on masked cells. Weak.

evidence.title: Universal multilayer network exploration by random walk with restart
evidence.claim: RWR propagates proximity from seeds over several hops and across layers and is validated by LOOCV. Combining layers helped in the gene-disease task: gene multiplex plus disease monoplex beat PPI alone and the gene multiplex alone. The drug layer with low bipartite overlap added nothing, while the airport layer with high overlap helped. The paper does not state that layers help only when overlap is high in the gene-disease case.
evidence.system_side: Confirmed: imputation is the mean tier score of a member's direct neighbours on the cosponsor graph only (adjacency built at fec/stance/stance_dynamics.py:90), with at least 5 neighbours (MINNB) and absolute estimate at least 0.75 (CONF). HCoI is used only for the co-movement test. The proposal file data/stance/stance_imputation_proposals.csv has 308 lines including the header, so 307 proposals is reproduced. The 77% masking sign agreement was not reproduced.
evidence.transfer: A per-member RWR seeded on known stances could replace the one-hop mean, and the existing masking protocol already has the form of LOOCV. Neighbour co-movement was null, so a multi-hop walk may not help either. This is a candidate needing a prereg and a single look, not evidence. Stance labels are Paul's domain: proposals only, and the matrix is never edited.

evidence.title: A Network-Based Measure of Cosponsorship Influence on Bill Passing in the United States House of Representatives
evidence.claim: The 6-month half-life is one of three settings for decaying cosponsorship-influence capital, not a stance-salience estimate. Discrimination barely changes between 6 and 24 months (0.248 vs 0.203).
evidence.system_side: Media blend decays each post by 0.5^(age/HL): HL 2.0 years for press and SOCIAL_HL_YEARS default 0.5 for social (confirmed in build_media_blend.py).
evidence.transfer: Not transferable. The paper's decay applies to accrued passage-rate ties and its outcome is bill passage. Its flatness across half-lives warns against treating any one value as calibrated. The paper does not justify 0.5 years for social posts or 2 years for press.

evidence.title: Big data-assisted social media analytics for business model for business decision making system competitive analysis
evidence.claim: Scores phrase sentiment with the general-purpose Affin lexicon plus an ensemble classifier for praise vs complaint. Accuracy is described as 'highest' with no metric, and the Affin citation points to an unrelated photonics paper.
evidence.system_side: Tone intensity is the LSD2015 charge (pos+neg)/words with negation handling, used as intensity only. Direction comes from the stance readers.
evidence.transfer: There is no evidence here that a general lexicon measures tone validly on congressional press releases. The open question (does LSD intensity agree with human-coded intensity?) is untouched. Rice & Zorn's case for domain dictionaries remains the relevant source.

evidence.title: Inferring social networks from unstructured text data: A proof of concept detection of hidden communities of interest
evidence.claim: HCoI ties are links from thematic similarity of texts, mediated by the texts rather than social ties. The paper does not discuss stance, agreement or change in agreement.
evidence.system_side: stance_dynamics.py runs a neighbour co-movement test on HCoI same-community pairs (lines 111-121). Imputation proposals use only cosponsor adjacency; hadj is used only in the co-movement test. Thresholds: at least 5 neighbours (SD_MINNB) and confidence at least 0.75 (SD_CONF). The stored stance_dynamics.json co_movement block reads same 134, opposite 122, which is 52 percent with no layer label, so the 49 percent null is not reproduced.
evidence.transfer: The paper's silence on stance supports keeping HCoI out of stance imputation only as an argument from the construct, not from the paper's evidence. The null result needs a labelled layer in the output before it is cited.

evidence.title: Measuring stance dynamics in political debate using temporal graph neural networks
evidence.claim: Stance is tracked as a trajectory over 28-day snapshots, with embedding persistence so silent users keep a stance. Movement is sorted into seven dynamics using a static band of median plus MAD. Mirror-image O-to-S and S-to-O flip curves suggest external events. Users with no direct stance are predicted through graph propagation over their neighbours.
evidence.system_side: Module docstring (lines 3-21) states the transplant. Code confirms 91-day default windows (line 26), last observed stance carried through silent windows (lines 48-55), the seven-dynamics classifier (lines 64-67), flip curves (lines 72-84), cosponsor and HCoI co-movement (lines 94-120), and CSV-only imputation proposals that leave the matrix untouched (lines 132-151). Re-run on the press CSV in scratch: 2,388 rows, 373 members, 18 windows.
evidence.transfer: The design vocabulary transfers. The paper says the mirror symmetry suggests external events; it does not establish an event detector the module can rely on. The paper's neighbour inference is GNN message passing over learned embeddings, not a copy rule, so the system's neighbour-based imputation is an analogue only.

evidence.title: Measuring stance dynamics in political debate using temporal graph neural networks
evidence.claim: The median plus MAD static band is applied to continuous stance values p in [-1,1] from the MLP, computed over all users' absolute changes. The paper gives no condition that users must post in nearly every period; its 10-tweet filter only implies about one interaction per snapshot on average.
evidence.system_side: Band is computed on observed-to-observed transitions only, from confidence-weighted means of stance_sign in {-1,0,+1}, floored at 0.05 (code lines 56-63). Live static_band 0.7076 is reproduced. Of 2,989 transitions, 2,737 (91.6 percent) are static and 252 move: S-to-O 111, O-to-S 43, S-to-MS 88 (a move with no sign change), S-to-LS 7, O-to-LO 2, O-to-MO 1 (flip_curves in stance_dynamics.json, matching the scratch re-run).
evidence.transfer: The band means what the paper intends only where stance is continuous and densely observed. With pooled quarterly signs it mainly measures how coarse the labels are. The paper gives no support for the seven-class counts. The within-side classes are rare because a move must exceed about 0.71 on a [-1,1] scale; they are not empty by construction.

evidence.title: Measuring stance dynamics in political debate using temporal graph neural networks
evidence.claim: Neighbour co-movement: users shift in the same direction as their 1-hop and 2-hop neighbours (diagonal dominance in Fig. 6). The authors describe tight-knit communities moving together, call it a descriptive correlation, and report no null model and no identification. The text gives no numbers; values appear only in the heatmaps.
evidence.system_side: Co-movement counts same versus opposite direction for neighbours who both move in a window. Diagonal dominance is declared above 0.55 (code line 106). Cosponsor result as stored: same 134, opposite 122, 52.3 percent, below threshold, so null. The HCoI figure of 49 percent cited in the rel is not stored in stance_dynamics.json. Scratch re-run on the current press_hcoi.json gives same 302, opposite 296, 50.5 percent, also below threshold. No permutation or common-shock control exists.
evidence.transfer: The paper's result is a descriptive correlation at 28-day resolution on Twitter, not evidence of influence. Do not carry the paper's potential social influences wording or its asymmetric social influence signals claim into system text. A null on one layer is a null on that layer only.

evidence.title: Measuring stance dynamics in political debate using temporal graph neural networks
evidence.claim: Silent-user inference is validated with 5-fold cross-validation over annotated users. For validation users, all edges to referendum-labelled hashtags are removed before training and inference. Scoring is macro-F1 per period on that period's validation users, chosen over accuracy because of class imbalance. Reported TWLGCN levels are steady between 70 and 90 percent.
evidence.system_side: Imputation takes the mean tier score of at least 5 cosponsor neighbours (MINNB=5, line 132) and keeps blank member-issue cells with |est| at least 0.75 (CONF, line 132). Masking check compares the neighbour estimate sign with the known label sign on confident cells only: 77.5 percent on n=1,087 (stance_dynamics.json). Proposals: 307 (CSV has 308 lines including header). True Neutral (score 0) counts as a negative sign (line 143). The final print says at least 3 informative neighbors while the threshold is 5 (line 152). No party-only or majority-class baseline, no macro-F1, no retraining, no 5-fold split.
evidence.transfer: The paper's protocol retrains a model with masked own-edges and reports macro-F1 across folds. The system's check is a neighbour-only estimate scored by raw sign agreement on a confidence-selected subset. Call it an analogue. The 77.5 percent is not comparable to the paper's macro-F1 range and stays UNVERIFIED (DE-062) until a party or majority baseline is run.

evidence.title: Measuring stance dynamics in political debate using temporal graph neural networks
evidence.claim: Carrying learned embeddings and MLP weights forward between snapshots beats re-initialising each period, by 1.3 to 9.8 percent on Exit_DS. The 28-day window was chosen by a sensitivity analysis on giant-component fraction: shorter windows fragment the graph and longer ones mask rapid shifts.
evidence.system_side: Persistence carries the last observed raw stance into silent windows (lines 48-55), not learned embeddings. Carried windows also enter transition counts (lines 69-73), which inflates static counts and credits flips to the window where posting resumes. The 91-day default (line 26) is justified by an analogy comment about quarters, with no sensitivity run.
evidence.transfer: The paper's persistence gain is for warm-started learned representations that keep updating from new edges. It does not support freezing a categorical label. The window rule can be borrowed, but it needs per-window graphs the press corpus does not supply. Fig. S2 is in the supplement and was not checked.

evidence.title: Large Language Model Enhanced Logic Tensor Network for Stance Detection
evidence.claim: FOL rules elicited from an LLM (Table 5 bike-lane rule links congestion to Against) are made differentiable with soft-logic operators: negation 1-U, conjunction U1*U2, implication 1-U1+U1*U2 (Eqs 2-5), and trained end to end with cross-entropy (Eq 12). Zero-shot VAST all-class F_avg: 81.0 vs 76.8 for KASD with 100 percent training data (+4.2); 80.2 vs 74.0 for MPPT with 10 percent (+6.2). Error analysis of 50 VAST errors (Sec 4.8) names LLM over-inference that links a positive clause to the target, and clause-level polarity conflicts.
evidence.system_side: compose() in apply_two_hop_stance.py is a hard sign flip: support with positive valence stays support, and the reverse flips; neutral and unrelated pass through. lookup() takes the first registry entry whose match substring appears in target plus text, and the flat model alignment is the fallback on a miss (line 55). The file docstring reports stance-hop 0.915, valence-hop 0.689 and oracle ceiling 0.872, and the eval prints a flat baseline of 0.677. The composed 0.782 and F1 0.754 and the claim that every automatic-registry variant fell below the flat baseline are not in the cited code.
evidence.transfer: Transfer is limited to the decomposition idea. FOLAR targets are benchmark targets, whereas the valence hop needs CU-specific, owner-judged knowledge that LLM priors do not supply. The paper's over-inference failure matches the automatic-registry failure in the system. LLM-elicited valence rules stay UNVERIFIED (DE-062) until scored against the 400 tweet golds under single-look rules. The paper gives no evidence that a soft operator beats an exact registry lookup where the registry has coverage.

evidence.title: Large Language Model Enhanced Logic Tensor Network for Stance Detection
evidence.claim: Fusing decisions from three LLMs (GPT-3.5-turbo-0301, Claude-2-100k, LLaMA-2-70b-chat) by attention-based routing (Eqs 7-11) beats a single-GPT-3.5 variant: 81.0 vs 75.2 on zero-shot VAST with 100 percent training data (+5.8), and 80.2 vs 74.9 with 10 percent (+5.3). The authors say LLMs often exhibit bias in knowledge elicitation that varies with training data and methods.
evidence.system_side: stage5_debate.py is zero-shot: the Political DEBATE base model (mlburnham/Political_DEBATE_base_v1.0) runs through a zero-shot-classification pipeline with hypothesis template 'This text is {}.' (line 31), and no training code appears in the file. claude_stance.py defaults to claude-sonnet-4-6 (line 32) and asks for a reason of at most 15 words (line 25). Its docstring calls the ensemble member a fine-tuned DEBATE and says the Claude pre-labels are corrected by a person. The 552-label training set and 87.2 percent agreement are not in the cited files.
evidence.transfer: The paper's ablation confounds fusion with the number of LLMs (one versus three), so it does not isolate a fusion effect, and no variance is reported. The benchmark inputs are tweets for SEM16 and ISD, while the paper does not describe VAST's source text and gives no collection dates, so a 2016-2020 framing is unsupported. The named model snapshots are the paper's choices; their retirement is not checked here. A second LLM rater would expose labeller-specific bias before human override, but the evidence is weak and new agent output stays UNVERIFIED (DE-062).

evidence.title: Large Language Model Enhanced Logic Tensor Network for Stance Detection
evidence.claim: In-target (Table 3): FOLAR beats the best competitor by 1.7 on LA (72.7 vs COLA 71.0) and by 2.0 on DT_I (73.3 vs MPPT 71.3), but trails KEprompt on FM (70.6 vs 72.1). Zero-shot (Table 4): gains of +4.2 on VAST with 100 percent training data and +6.2 with 10 percent. The baselines include statistical, PLM, prompt and LLM methods. No TF-IDF or SVM baseline is reported.
evidence.system_side: train_tweet_stance.py grids LinearSVC and LogReg over word plus char TF-IDF (lines 31-40) and scores by 5-fold stratified CV over the tweet golds (lines 42-54). The file docstring cites 400 golds. The file has no untouched test split. The figures 83.9 percent, macro-F1 0.816 on an untouched n=87 test, and 0.737 CV on 399 golds are not in the cited code and were not checked.
evidence.transfer: The paper cannot settle SVM versus LLM for this corpus because it runs no bag-of-words baseline. Its pattern (small in-target gains, larger low-data or new-target gains) suggests an LLM-rule reader would help most on new or rare CU targets, which has not been tested for CU stance. The evidence is benchmark-level, rests on three runs and gives no confidence intervals.

evidence.title: A cost-minimized two-stage three-way dynamic consensus mechanism for social network-large scale group decision-making: Utilizing K-nearest neighbors for incomplete fuzzy preference relations
evidence.claim: Missing preference entries are imputed from the K=4 most trusted neighbours with a known value. Each weight blends trust and preference similarity (mu = (t + sim)/(1 + sim), then normalized), and entries are filled in order of reliability r and iterated to convergence. In the worked case f10_45 = 0.4033 comes from 4 neighbours weighted 0.2549/0.2507/0.2503/0.2440, the highest-reliability gap (r = 3.8683) of 39 missing entries. Imputation MSE stays at 0.09-0.13 across p in {20..100}, n in {4..12} and missing rates 0.1/0.2/0.3, on synthetic data only.
evidence.system_side: The silent-member proposer takes each member's cosponsor neighbours as an UNWEIGHTED binary adjacency set (edge weights are dropped when the Edges sheet is read). It averages the neighbours' tier scores per category, with no similarity weighting, no reliability ordering and no iteration. It proposes a cell only when there are at least 5 neighbours (SD_MINNB) and |est| >= 0.75 (SD_CONF). It checks sign agreement on cells whose stance is already known, with no party-only baseline, and outputs proposals only. The same script reports co-movement as null on cosponsor ties.
evidence.transfer: Only the mechanics carry over: neighbour weights from tie strength plus profile similarity, and filling the best-supported gaps first. The paper's evidence does not transfer. Its MSE comes from random synthetic matrices; its trust network is elicited trust among decision-makers, not cosponsorship; its alternatives are 5 investment options, not legislators' CU stance categories. Its homophily premise is assumed, never tested, while this system measured co-movement as null on cosponsor ties. A weighted variant should be adopted only if a masked-cell test beats both the current unweighted mean and a party-only baseline on held-out members. Until a second path reproduces that result it stays UNVERIFIED (DE-062). Weights must be labelled heuristic tie strength, never trust or closeness (D-025).

evidence.title: Social network group decision making: Characterization, taxonomy, challenges and future directions from an AI and LLMs perspective
evidence.claim: SNGDM consensus mechanisms model opinion updating along trust edges with DeGroot and Hegselmann-Krause dynamics (refs 9 and 71). The review treats network-driven opinion convergence as the core mechanism but reports no test of it.
evidence.system_side: Neighbour imputation takes an unweighted mean of neighbours' tier scores, which is one DeGroot-style averaging step. It requires at least 5 neighbours (MINNB) and |est| >= 0.75 (CONF), and it only proposes values without changing the matrix. Measured co-movement on the cosponsor and HCoI layers was null.
evidence.transfer: DeGroot assumes that neighbours' opinions move a node's opinion. That holds by design in elicited SNGDM panels. The system's own null co-movement result means the assumption is not supported on congressional layers. This paper adds no evidence either way, so the imputation stays a proposal-only heuristic.

evidence.title: Negative Link Prediction in Social Media
evidence.claim: Signed triads are overwhelmingly balanced: 92.31 percent (Epinions) and 93.01 percent (Slashdot) of undirected triads (Sec. 3.2 p. 89). This is a structural prior that sign products usually hold in person-to-person trust networks. The paper does not test stance-times-valence composition.
evidence.system_side: Sign logic confirmed: compose(stance, v) returns support when stance is support and v is positive, and when stance is oppose and v is negative; it returns oppose for the other two combinations. Correction: compose() sets no cu_alignment variable; cu_alignment appears only as CSV column names (lines 37, 55-56). The 0.872 oracle ceiling and 0.677 flat baseline are in the file docstring. The 0.782 registry two-hop score (tweet_stance_stack.py docstring) is measured on the 400 tweet golds the design iterated against, not 5-fold CV; the 5-fold out-of-fold claim applies to the stacked model.
evidence.transfer: Paper triads are person-to-person links. The system's third node is an interest reached through a curated valence registry. The paper supplies only a structural prior and does not validate the registry. The registry numbers are on the golds the design iterated against, so they are not an out-of-sample validation.

evidence.title: Adversarial Attack on Graph Neural Networks as An Influence Maximization Problem
evidence.claim: Perturbing features of only 1 percent of nodes, chosen by an influence-maximization criterion, sharply lowers accuracy of GCN, GAT and JK-Net. Cora GAT falls from 87.7 (no attack) to 55.9 under InfMax-Unif at the 10 percent degree threshold. The paper's model (B = M^L) implies that propagation lets a few nodes affect many predictions; no propagation ablation is reported.
evidence.system_side: Neighbour imputation takes the one-hop mean TSCORE of at least 5 labelled cosponsor neighbours and keeps proposals with |est| at least 0.75. The masking validation sign agreement is stored in data/stance/stance_dynamics.json as 0.775 over n = 1087. Proposals go to a CSV only; the matrix is unchanged.
evidence.transfer: The system has no GNN and uses a one-hop mean with human adjudication, so propagation is shallow and an adversary is implausible. The transferable idea is a sensitivity test: flip or corrupt the labels of a few high-coverage members, chosen by walk coverage rather than at random, and count sign changes in the proposals. Any result stays UNVERIFIED until reproduced (DE-062). Weak.

evidence.title: Psychological Aspects of Natural Language Use: Our Words, Our Selves
evidence.claim: Emotion words are under 5 percent of words in daily speech, emotional writing and affect-laden poetry, so emotion-word counts predict emotional state weakly. Word-count programs cannot consider context, irony or sarcasm. In at least two studies, judges' ratings of emotionality correlated more highly with language use than with self-reports.
evidence.system_side: Per-release intensity is abs(lsd_net_norm) or lsd_charge = (pos + neg) / words, multiplied by the stance sign to give press_value, so intensity scales every press cell.
evidence.transfer: The paper claim concerns personal emotional state, not how heated a policy release is. LSD2015 is a sentiment dictionary (Young and Soroka 2012 per file header), not LIWC. The sparsity point carries over: in short releases a few hits set the multiplier. The judge finding supports validating intensity against human coding.

evidence.claim: The connectivity to agreement link depends on whether the pair are expected allies or adversaries (bloc). Same-bloc dyads co-vote in 574 of 594 cases (about 97 percent), so H2 is untestable. For opposed-bloc pairs more contact predicts less co-voting (p. 625; Table 3).
evidence.system_side: Neighbour imputation takes the unweighted mean of TSCORE over every cosponsor neighbour, with at least 5 neighbours (SD_MINNB) and absolute estimate at least 0.75 (SD_CONF). It does not condition on party. Masking validation reports sign agreement but has no party-only baseline. The co-movement test on cosponsor and HCoI ties is reported as null.
evidence.transfer: The paper outcome is votes, not stance labels, so transfer is conceptual. The next diagnostic is a party-only baseline and a split of same-party from cross-party neighbours. The 77 percent figure stays UNVERIFIED as a network effect until that baseline exists (DE-062).

evidence.title: Comparing Fine-Tuned RoBERTa with Traditional Machine Learning Models for Stance Detection in Political Tweets
evidence.claim: Classical models on TF-IDF features rank RF 0.95 > SVM 0.94 > LR 0.93 > DT 0.92 > NB 0.89 on a 1,675-row test split. Fine-tuned RoBERTa on tweet plus comment paired input reports 0.97 accuracy on a support of 6,699 described as the augmented dataset. Augmentation and class balancing are credited with gains, but no with and without comparison is shown.
evidence.system_side: train_stance_domain.py is labelled as the Khan pipeline adapted to the CU domain. It builds a target-conditioned paired input, runs the same five classifiers with class_weight balanced, has an --augment flag that adds title and stance-span views to TRAIN only, and has a --transformer path defaulting to distilroberta-base with 4 epochs and inverse-frequency loss weights.
evidence.transfer: The mechanics (paired input, balanced loss, per-class P/R/F1 and macro-F1) transfer. The model ordering and the augmentation gain are not established by the paper: its classical rows are scored on 1,675 rows and its RoBERTa row on 6,699 rows. 6,699 is almost exactly 0.8 x 8,374 (6,699.2), the size of the 80 percent training share, so the RoBERTa figure may not be on a held-out set. The paper does not say which, so this is an inference and must be labelled as one.

evidence.title: Comparing Fine-Tuned RoBERTa with Traditional Machine Learning Models for Stance Detection in Political Tweets
evidence.claim: The transformer beats every classical model (0.97 vs at most 0.95). Dataset augmentation and class balancing are credited with improving performance, with no with and without comparison shown.
evidence.system_side: On the CU press gold set (per the analyst, 552 labelled rows, untouched test n=87), a transformer trained on augmented data reached 0.757 macro-F1, below a tuned word plus char LinearSVC at 0.816. The analyst reports the augmentation was rejected on 2026-07-03. Production uses the SVM.
evidence.transfer: The system numbers are single-look on an 87-row test and were not re-verified here. They are not a refutation of the paper's own measurement; they show that its ordering and augmentation gain did not transfer to this small English press corpus. Relation changed from contradicts to qualifies, because the paper's claim is about its own data.

evidence.title: Comparing Fine-Tuned RoBERTa with Traditional Machine Learning Models for Stance Detection in Political Tweets
evidence.claim: A fine-tuned RoBERTa reaches 0.97 accuracy on political stance. Misclassification concentrates in sarcastic, ambiguous and indirect statements, and some disagree-labelled items are predicted unrelated when explicit negation is absent.
evidence.system_side: The production transformer reader is Political DEBATE, an NLI-head model fine-tuned on about 552 labelled releases for 3 epochs. Per the analyst it scores 0.839 accuracy and kappa 0.742 held out, 0.571 on an adversarial frame, and the dominant error is implicit support read as neutral (n=78).
evidence.transfer: The error-mode finding (implicit and indirect stance is the residual failure) transfers and matches the system's neutral versus support seam. The 0.97 headline should not be a target or prior because it comes from a non-common evaluation set. The DEBATE reader is an NLI entailment model, not a RoBERTa classifier, so the architectures differ. Treat the paper as weak qualitative support only.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence and Sentiment Analysis: A Review in Competitive Research
evidence.claim: The paper asserts that AI understands the tone of a statement rather than just recognising words. Citing Alantari et al. 2022, it says neural-network ML gives the most accurate predictions of the text-based methods compared. The review reports no accuracy figures of its own, and its corpus is 43 business and competitive-research papers from 2012-2022.
evidence.system_side: A fine-tuned Political DEBATE NLI model (mlburnham/Political_DEBATE_base_v1.0) gives the CU stance direction. stance_sign is support, oppose or neutral, and the code states that this is independent of LSD tone. On held-out human gold it scored 0.839 accuracy / kappa 0.742 (n=87). It scored 0.796 on the 760-row frame and 0.571 on the adversarial goldeval frame.
evidence.transfer: Weak. The cited evidence covers consumer reviews and business social media, not congressional press releases. It also concerns sentiment polarity, not target-specific stance toward CU policy interests. It neither supports nor tests the system's validated accuracy, which comes from a stricter protocol (held-out, member-grouped human gold).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence and Sentiment Analysis: A Review in Competitive Research
evidence.claim: Alantari et al., as summarised by the review, find a trade-off: neural networks predict well but diagnose poorly, while more transparent methods are poorer predictors. The review frames word-matching approaches as the baseline that AI improves on. The trade-off is qualitative only and no numbers are given.
evidence.system_side: Lexicoder LSD2015 counts run with negation phrases removed first. They yield lsd_net_norm = net/words and lsd_charge = (pos+neg)/words. Only the magnitude (|net_norm| or charge) enters press_value = final_sign x intensity, so the dictionary sets intensity and never direction.
evidence.transfer: The paper agrees with the system's split of roles: an opaque predictive reader for direction and a transparent dictionary for an interpretable intensity scalar. It gives no evidence that dictionary intensity is valid on political press releases. The open question of whether LSD intensity matches human-coded intensity on this corpus is untouched. The source evidence is consumer reviews.

evidence.title: Is Bigger Always Better? Potential Biases of Big Data Derived from Social Network Sites
evidence.claim: Non-users are excluded from a site-based sampling frame by design. If selection is related to outcomes, results from users may reach the opposite conclusion about the wider population. Sampling should not be tied to the substantive question. The paper does not discuss how missing social-media activity should be coded.
evidence.system_side: build_media_blend.py: SOCIAL_W = 0.5; f = min(1, nz/15), with nz the members carrying a nonzero social value in the category (shrink on by default). Cell = (1 - 0.5f) x press/p80 + 0.5f x social/p80. A member with no social value gets sv = 0, so at f = 1 the press side is halved and silence scores as zero, not missing (confirmed at lines 29, 463, 479). The downstream Press Release - Raw link was not checked.
evidence.transfer: The paper gives no evidence about missing-data coding. The concern bites only if posters differ from non-posters on stance in categories where f = 1; that is untested, and the analyst's own note says so. The stance-ladder rule on missing evidence was not checked. UNVERIFIED.

evidence.title: How to train your stochastic parrot: large language models for political texts
evidence.claim: Continuous measures built from the label probability vector: per-sentence P(Conservative) minus P(Liberal), averaged per manifesto, gives rho 0.92 (economic) and 0.80 (social) across 18 UK manifestos with GPT-3. Tweet sentiment uses the first principal component of the positive/negative/neutral probability vector.
evidence.system_side: run_stage5.R:143 sets press_value = final_sign x intensity, where intensity is abs(lsd_net_norm) by default (line 141). final_sign is the bill sign or stance_sign, which is the argmax of DEBATE (run_stage5.R:140; stage5_debate.py:77-82). run_stage5.R:9 is a comment only. p_support, p_oppose and p_neutral are kept as columns (run_stage5.R:98,166) and do not enter press_value.
evidence.transfer: The paper evidence uses GPT-3 next-token probabilities on a few-shot prompt, not DEBATE NLI entailment scores. DEBATE runs with multi_label=True (stage5_debate.py:65), so its three scores are independent and do not sum to 1. A p_support minus p_oppose contrast is a different object and would need a pre-registered single look on the 760-row press gold. Remains UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it (DE-062).

evidence.title: How to train your stochastic parrot: large language models for political texts
evidence.claim: Tweets whose meaning depends on outside political context are misread unless the prompt supplies that context. The Masterpiece sentiment prompt included a preamble on the ruling and six few-shot examples, and GPT-3 got the sign right on 88.4 percent of 945 tweets.
evidence.system_side: The system described is claude_stance.py, not DEBATE. Its SYSTEM prompt (lines 19-23) carries a credit-union policy map and tells the model to judge by the member position on the underlying issue, not by the words credit union. Its docstring (lines 5-8) names it the pre-labeller and the third member of the ensemble, with the Credit Card Competition Act example.
evidence.transfer: The paper task is sentiment toward a court ruling, not stance toward an interest, so the paper gives no accuracy figure for CU stance. The paper used six few-shot examples; claude_stance.py is zero-shot with a policy map. The supported point is the design choice of supplying context in the prompt.

evidence.title: How to train your stochastic parrot: large language models for political texts
evidence.claim: GPT-4, tuned with RLHF, is poorly calibrated and overconfident. For over 70 percent of its posts it gave one label more than 99 percent probability, and it chose Neutral more often than the authors. GPT-4 was slightly worse than GPT-3 on sentiment and little or no better on ideology. Section 4 says newer RLHF models frequently underperform on classification and scaling tasks, and the latest model is not always the best.
evidence.system_side: claude_stance.py asks for a self-stated confidence from 0 to 1 in its JSON reply (line 25) and defaults to claude-sonnet-4-6 (line 32). A call that fails all 4 attempts stays neutral with confidence 0.0 and reason ERR (lines 80, 95-97). An unrecognised label is set to neutral (lines 89-91), but the stated confidence is still read at line 92, so it is not reset to 0.0.
evidence.transfer: These are GPT-3 and GPT-4 results, not Claude results. The module requests no token log-probabilities (none found in the file), so the paper probability-vector method cannot be applied as written. claude_conf is a self-stated number, not a calibrated probability. Neutral rows created by ERR should be counted apart from model-chosen neutral rows. No DEBATE-vs-Claude agreement figure was located in the sources checked.

evidence.title: How to train your stochastic parrot: large language models for political texts
evidence.claim: Dictionary methods lose badly when meaning depends on context. The best dictionary the authors could build got 38.3 percent of tweet signs right, against 88.4 percent for GPT-3. Of 5332 speeches containing honor, GPT-3 labels only 145 as praising honor.
evidence.system_side: LSD2015 is used only for intensity. run_stage5.R:141 takes abs(lsd_net_norm) by default, or lsd_charge when CU_S5_INTENSITY=charge, and line 143 multiplies it by final_sign. stage5_lsd.R (header lines 10-15) matches and removes negation phrases before counting. Direction in run_stage5.R comes from the DEBATE stance with bill-sign and human-label overrides (lines 139-140), not from the Claude rater.
evidence.transfer: The paper dictionary is the authors own construction, not LSD2015, and the paper did not test intensity. Intensity inherits the context blindness the paper describes (ceremonial or quoted language reads as heated). Whether LSD intensity tracks human-coded intensity is untested.

evidence.title: Emerging Late Adolescent Friendship Networks and Big Five Personality Traits: A Social Network Approach
evidence.claim: Stochastic actor-oriented models estimate tie selection conditional on the current network state, with ego, alter and similarity terms for each covariate, and pool groups by multilevel meta-analysis. The cited extensions (Steglich et al. 2006; Burk et al. 2007) model networks and behaviour together, which separates selection from influence.
evidence.system_side: Neighbour co-movement counts members who move in the same versus the opposite direction as their cosponsor or HCoI neighbours, quarter to quarter. The result was null on both layers. Neighbour imputation proposals are built on this (77% sign agreement under masking).
evidence.transfer: Transfer is moderate in method only. The paper itself models selection and not influence, so it gives no evidence on stance contagion. A joint network-and-behaviour SIENA model is the standard way to ask whether ties drive stance change or stance similarity drives ties. That would need panel waves of cosponsor ties and quarterly stances. It would be new analysis, UNVERIFIED until reproduced, and its pooled estimates must be reported by stratum (party, chamber) or marked UNSTRATIFIED.

evidence.title: Party Cues in the News: Democratic Elites, Republican Backlash and the Dynamics of Climate Skepticism
evidence.claim: The authors use Lexicoder with a custom dictionary of party names, office titles and party leaders to detect party cues, not sentiment or tone. They validate detection against hand coding of a random 700 articles (about 80% contain a cue by their definition). Stance is hand-coded on a separate random sample of 3000 articles (97% of articles with Democratic messages are wholly pro-consensus). Frames come from SVM classifiers (77-80% accuracy).
evidence.system_side: stage5_lsd.R runs the LSD2015 dictionary in lsd_tone (lines 49-60), returning net tone and charge per word. Live run_stage5.R defaults the intensity to the absolute net tone per word (INTENSITY default net_norm, line 45), with charge only as an option, and press_value equals final_sign times that intensity at lines 141-143. The bearing's earlier statement that charge per word is the intensity used in press_value was wrong.
evidence.transfer: The paper is a method precedent only: a dictionary for detecting actors plus hand-coded validation. It never uses or validates sentiment or tone as an intensity measure, so it is no evidence that LSD tone intensity is valid on congressional press releases.

evidence.title: Pitch Perfect: Vocal Pitch and the Emotional Intensity of Congressional Speech
evidence.claim: Speech topic, word choice and length of remarks are highly controllable and driven by strategic concerns, while vocal pitch typically lies beyond the individual's control, making it a more honest indicator of intensity on a given issue (leakage hierarchy, pp. 942-944). The paper does not compare dictionary tone or LSD scores with pitch.
evidence.system_side: Press intensity is |LSD net| / words or (pos + neg) / words (lsd_charge) per member press release. The press pillar multiplies stance sign by this heat.
evidence.transfer: A theoretical argument only; the paper never tests LSD tone against pitch. The claim that press releases are staff-drafted and so more strategic than floor speech has no support in the paper or the code. LSD charge measures crafted rhetorical tone, not felt intensity, and should be labelled that way.

evidence.title: Corpus-Based Dictionaries for Sentiment Analysis of Specialized Vocabularies
evidence.claim: General-purpose dictionaries carry valences that are wrong in specialized vocabularies (tennis 'love'). On the movie-review benchmark a corpus-derived dictionary reached 80.4% in-sample and 79.5% held-out, versus LIWC 69.4% and AFINN 71.3% in-sample and AFINN 70.6% held-out.
evidence.system_side: Stage 5b scores full release bodies with the stock LSD2015 dictionary (1,709 positive and 2,858 negative entries; counts verified against LSDaug2015.zip). Intensity = abs(pos-neg)/words. Verified entries: 'credit' family (credit, credits, credited, creditable, crediting) is positive; debt*, charge*, risk*, oversight* and fraud* are negative. No domain masking in run_stage5.R:79. The local masking figures (4.5% and 7.0% of mass, rho 0.953, 4.1% sign flips, press_value rho 0.976) were NOT reproduced here: no R runtime, and the text cache is R rds only.
evidence.transfer: The paper's evidence covers polarity classification of movie reviews and court opinions, not intensity and not congressional press releases. The mechanism (domain nouns read as tone) is visible directly in the LSD entries. Size of the effect on releases remains UNVERIFIED in this pass. The paper does not test whether LSD intensity tracks human-judged heat.

evidence.title: Corpus-Based Dictionaries for Sentiment Analysis of Specialized Vocabularies
evidence.claim: Polarity = (sum Wp - sum Wn)/(sum Wp + sum Wn), with Wp and Wn built from tf-idf and cosine-weighted counts over 500 positive and 500 negative words taken from 300-dimensional GloVe vectors (window 50, minimum count 90) trained on the domain corpus, seeded by 10 positive and 10 negative words. Gains over LIWC and AFINN already appear at 5,000 documents, rise steeply to about 15,000, and show marginal gains after 30,000.
evidence.system_side: Formula at cu_press_release_scraper.R:2799 matches (Wp-Wn)/(Wp+Wn). Wp and Wn come from the hand-curated TONE_LEXICON, whose weights are 1, 2 and 3 (confirmed), not corpus-derived cosine or tf-idf weights. expand_tone_lexicon() (line 2490 onward) departs from the paper: GloVe rank 50 (paper 300), window 5 (paper 50), term_count_min 5 (paper 90), a bipolar axis, 200 terms per side (paper 500), different seeds, 50-document floor. lexicon_candidates.csv is absent, consistent with never having run. The 2026-06-21 supersede claim (21 of 32 neutral releases) is unsupported in files checked (UNVERIFIED).
evidence.transfer: The formula transfers as written. The paper's validity evidence applies only to corpus-derived, similarity-weighted dictionaries, which this code does not build. The paper's own accuracy gains start at 5,000 documents; the CU-relevant set is 1,563 text-bearing releases. Paper says document-level polarity hides subject (p.27), which supports the stance split.

evidence.title: Corpus-Based Dictionaries for Sentiment Analysis of Specialized Vocabularies
evidence.claim: Changing the dictionary reorders units. Justice-level rank correlations are 0.29 (corpus measure vs LIWC) and 0.16 (corpus measure vs AFINN), versus 0.64 between LIWC and AFINN. Standard deviation of justice means is 0.25 (corpus), 0.22 (LIWC) and 0.16 (AFINN). Justices with more than 50 majority opinions; comparison across 84 justices.
evidence.system_side: press_value = final_sign x abs(lsd_net_norm), or lsd_charge when INTENSITY is charge (run_stage5.R:141-143, verified). Member and category roll-up uses decay weights (cu_press_release_scraper.R:154-158 comment). The Press pillar normalization is signed-extrema in fec/moneyball_core.py:214-237 (verified as normalization, not as press_value roll-up). Only one instrument is used; no alternative is compared.
evidence.transfer: The divergence evidence comes from a 217-year court corpus with large semantic drift. Press releases from 2022 on are a narrow window, so the divergence is probably smaller there; that is the analyst's inference and is untested. The live blend press weight of 0.10 was not checked in this pass.

evidence.title: Machine and deep learning for personality traits detection: a comprehensive survey and open research challenges
evidence.claim: Traditional ML (SVM and similar on TF-IDF) remains interpretable and competitive on small data. Deep and transformer gains appear with large labeled corpora. The text claims about a 25% LSTM gain over traditional ML, but no table supports the figure.
evidence.system_side: The best classical stance reader is LinearSVC on word (1-2 gram) plus char_wb (3-5 gram) TF-IDF: 83.9% accuracy and macro-F1 .816 on 87 untouched test rows, versus a transformer at 0.757 on the same comparison. Supervised tweet stance reached 0.737 CV on 399 golds.
evidence.transfer: The paper studies personality, not stance, so this is a pattern about small labeled sets of a few hundred rows, not stance evidence. It fits the system's measured outcome. It does not show that transformers lose at larger n, and it says nothing about LLM zero-shot readers (Birkenmaier, Kim J.), which Paul's view rests on.

evidence.title: Automatic construction of direction-aware sentiment lexicon using direction-dependent words
evidence.claim: On four FPB subsets (DS50 4,835 / DS66 4,209 / DS75 3,447 / DS100 2,259 sentences) LM+Senti-DD weighted F1 is 0.7057, 0.7322, 0.7788, 0.8233 vs LM alone 0.5914, 0.6023, 0.6174, 0.5982. On SemEval-2017 (960 messages) and FiQA (436 sentences) it is 0.4789 and 0.4937, below several general lexicons. In the 20-case DS100 appendix sample 10 are correct and 10 wrong; cited failures include (profit, increase) and (company, increase).
evidence.system_side: Sign comes from DEBATE or the human overlay for text-bearing releases; the bill table supplies sign only for text-less billstatus rows (run_stage5.R lines 128-143). The directional-verb override derived from this paper was tested on whole release text and rejected (3 good / 43 bad sign changes on gold, per brain note). run_stage5.R lines 105-108 document a different rejected experiment (bill-sign override, accuracy 0.839 to 0.770, 2026-06-30) that the rel did not cite.
evidence.transfer: Evidence transfers only where a directional word governs the target noun inside one short sentence, as in FPB headlines. It does not transfer to whole-release counting over multi-actor congressional press text, where speaker attitude toward the direction is a second hop the paper does not model. The paper's own shift to SemEval and FiQA drops lexicon F1 below 0.5. This supports restricting any rule to the sentence naming the bill; any such variant stays UNVERIFIED until a held-out gold look (DE-062).

evidence.title: Automatic construction of direction-aware sentiment lexicon using direction-dependent words
evidence.claim: Polarity attaches to a (direction, target) pair. Direction-dependent nouns are typed proportional or inversely proportional by PMI against direction-tagged sentences (Eq. 1, delta = 0). Of 719 tagged sentences, 691 are proportional and 28 inversely proportional, and the imbalance yields noisy words such as beer and day.
evidence.system_side: Valence is attached per target family in derive_valence_registry.py. cfpb_institution and cfpb_general are fixed at 0 by user-directed policy and act as binding overrides. cfpb_reform and cfpb_expansion have no hard-coded sign; they take whatever sign the gold labels derive. The code keeps families at 75 percent gold consistency (min_consist=0.75) although the file header says 80 percent. Brain note: CFPB is 64% inverse under sentence-level typing and 41% under release-level typing (share of inverse tags, not accuracy). The gold-derived registry scores 0.782 accuracy in honest 5-fold CV against a flat 0.677 baseline; five auto-registry variants scored 0.464 to 0.604.
evidence.transfer: Paul's registry is a gold-derived analogue of the paper's direction-pair lexicon; the automatic PMI typing is the part that did not transfer. Transfer is limited by scale: 400 tweet golds and 238 distinct targets, against the paper's 4,835 sentences with a 1 percent noun-frequency floor. A PMI typing pass on this corpus needs a held-out look before any claim (DE-062).

evidence.title: Automatic construction of direction-aware sentiment lexicon using direction-dependent words
evidence.claim: Direction plus noun carries polarity that a general or finance dictionary misses. LM alone labels 'Profit for the period was EUR 10.9 mn, down from EUR 14.3 mn in 2009' neutral (SentimentScore 0), while the (profit, down) pair gives refined score -1. On DS100, negative-class F1 is 0.4087 for LM alone and 0.7260 for LM+Senti-DD.
evidence.system_side: LSD2015 tone in stage5_lsd.R is a direction-blind count of positive and negative words and negation phrases. Press intensity is |net|/words or charge, multiplied by the DEBATE or human sign, so LSD sets magnitude only and its sign is discarded. For text-less bill rows intensity is a fixed BILL_W (0.03).
evidence.transfer: Weak. LSD sign is discarded here, so the paper's flips matter for intensity only when directional pairs cancel or inflate |net|, as in cost-cut or fee-reduce releases. The paper tests neither LSD nor intensity, and Paul's system has no human-coded intensity gold to test this against.

evidence.title: Sentiment analysis of political communication: combining a dictionary approach with crowdcoding
evidence.claim: Validation on 200 sentences: aggregated lay crowd vs aggregated expert r = 0.82. Domain dictionary vs expert r = 0.65 at 84% coverage, about 0.6 when the 32 unmatched sentences are set to zero. Momtazi r = 0.13 (46% coverage) and SentiWS r = 0.19 (31% coverage). Authors state that dictionary analysis requires a customized dictionary and recommend caution with general-purpose dictionaries.
evidence.system_side: press_value tone intensity is stock LSD2015, uncustomized. stage5_lsd.R lsd_tone (lines 48-61) removes negator-plus-word hits and flips them: negated negatives count as positive and negated positives as negative. lsd_net_norm = (pos - neg) / words. run_stage5.R line 141 takes abs(lsd_net_norm) as heat; line 143 sets press_value = final_sign x heat. The brain note at debate-stance-model.md line 102 records only a three-case smoke test (pro +4 / negated 0 / neutral 0) and calls LSD validated, (a functional check by the paper standard).
evidence.transfer: The validation protocol transfers: about 200 releases rated 0-4 by lay coders and experts, correlated with |lsd_net_norm|. The size of the generic-dictionary penalty does not transfer directly, because the paper's comparators are machine-translated German lexicons, not LSD2015. This paper does not establish that LSD2015 performs well on English news; the Young and Soroka citation is general sentiment work, not an LSD validation. The paper scores sentences for negativity only, while LSD here is bidirectional and scores whole release bodies.

evidence.title: Sentiment analysis of political communication: combining a dictionary approach with crowdcoding
evidence.claim: Sentence tonality is set by the single most negative dictionary word (max rule). A negator immediately before a word excludes that word, and an intensifier multiplies it by 1.25. Word scores are crowd-derived means on a 0-4 scale. Mean word scores with the max rule and booster/negation handling give r = 0.65 (n = 168 test sentences). Other aggregation combinations give r from 0.38 to 0.58.
evidence.system_side: The graded layer header in cu_press_release_scraper.R cites Haselmayer and Jenny and says sentence tonality follows the strongest cue. The code does not: weighted_tone (about lines 2443-2475) sums every fired cue across all CU sentences into Wp and Wn, and graded_from_signed buckets |Wp - Wn| by GRADED_CUTS. The negator window covers two preceding tokens; a 0.75 downtoner is added (line 139), not in the paper. TONE_LEXICON has 44 hand-weighted entries (weights 1, 2, 3), not crowd-derived scores. run_stage5.R lines 146-160 reuse the magnitude only for display score_label; press_value does not use it.
evidence.transfer: This is a fidelity finding, not an empirical one. It matters for the display score_label magnitude and the comparison column only, because press_value and the press pillar do not consume the graded layer. No external claim that these graded labels follow Haselmayer and Jenny should be made.

evidence.title: Strategic identity signaling in heterogeneous networks
evidence.claim: Covert tweets were defined partly by moderates rating them neutral in orientation and affect while far copartisans saw political content; the authors argue automated political-speech classifiers will likely detect only overt speech and miss covert signals.
evidence.system_side: The DEBATE NLI reader picks the argmax over three hypotheses, and the neutral label is literally 'neutral toward or not about credit unions', mapped to sign 0. Coded or hedged support lands in the same zero bin as off-topic text, and no hedged or coded class exists.
evidence.transfer: Holds only if members code CU positions for mixed constituencies. The paper's covertness concerns partisan identity on a left-right axis among ordinary Twitter users, and CU issues are comparatively bipartisan, so the size of any neutral-bin leakage in congressional press is unknown. The classifier warning is the authors' conjecture, not a tested result.

evidence.title: Stance Detection: A Practical Guide to Classifying Political Beliefs in Text
evidence.claim: Ambiguity is 34.0 percent when Trump is not mentioned versus 19.5 percent when he is. NLI classifiers degrade most in low-context documents, while supervised and in-context classifiers adapt better.
evidence.system_side: Zero-shot DEBATE base read 53 percent accuracy and oppose F1 0.08 on the 156-row test. Fine-tuning on CU labels gave 87.2 percent accuracy and oppose F1 0.78 against the Claude reference. Figures trace to the vault note debate-stance-model and the 2026-06-22 topic note, not to code.
evidence.transfer: The paper measured Trump approval with generic DeBERTaV3 NLI, not Political DEBATE on CU press releases. Transfer to CU is by analogy.

evidence.title: Stance Detection: A Practical Guide to Classifying Political Beliefs in Text
evidence.claim: Zero-shot MCC for DeBERTaV3 Small is 0.15, Base 0.40 and Large 0.65 (83 percent accuracy). Performance comparable to supervised classifiers emerges only in larger models.
evidence.system_side: Production runs the Political DEBATE base model fine-tuned on 552 labeled rows for 3 epochs. The large model was never fine-tuned or scored on the same member-grouped test; the vault lists the large fine-tune as a next step.
evidence.transfer: The paper gap is for generic zero-shot NLI. Political DEBATE is a politics-trained model not studied in this paper, so the size gap may differ.

evidence.title: Stance Detection: A Practical Guide to Classifying Political Beliefs in Text
evidence.claim: In-context LLMs are useful for expanding training data and for validation, but not as the primary label source because proprietary models cannot be archived. The paper reports GPT-4 MCC 0.78 in Table 5 and recommends temperature zero in Section 4.3.4.
evidence.system_side: The fine-tune label is human_label when valid, otherwise the Claude pre_label. The Claude rater uses claude-sonnet-4-6 with no temperature argument. The 87.2 percent headline is agreement with Claude.
evidence.transfer: Applies to any training row whose human_label is empty. The share of Claude-only rows is not counted in the analysis.

evidence.title: Stance Detection: A Practical Guide to Classifying Political Beliefs in Text
evidence.claim: Bag-of-words LR, RF and SVM reach MCC 0.49-0.51 and RoBERTa, BERTweet and PoliBERTweet reach 0.60, 0.63 and 0.68 on Twitter. Laurer et al. 2024 found 500 training examples let language models outperform algorithms trained on several thousand.
evidence.system_side: Production is a LinearSVC on word plus char TF-IDF. Vault notes give 83.9 percent accuracy, but the 0.816 macro-F1 is a leak-free figure paired with an 84.7 percent headline, and other notes give 0.792 and 0.835 for the same model. The NLI-fine-tuned DEBATE reached 0.839 accuracy and 0.835 macro-F1 on n=87, which matches the vault. A distilroberta macro-F1 of 0.757 was not located.
evidence.transfer: With 456 training rows and an 87-row test all readers fall within each other's intervals. The paper's ordering is for larger training sets and for MCC, not macro-F1.

evidence.title: Stance Detection: A Practical Guide to Classifying Political Beliefs in Text
evidence.claim: Stance and sentiment are distinct dimensions to be measured independently. Sentiment may inform intensity but cannot stand in for stance. Integrating sentiment to scale stance intensity is named as a future direction needing more research.
evidence.system_side: press_value = stance sign times LSD intensity (|net| per word). The sign comes from DEBATE or the human overlay, never from the dictionary.
evidence.transfer: This is a conceptual endorsement of separating the two dimensions only. The paper does not test whether multiplying sign by intensity improves measurement; it calls that open.

evidence.title: Stance Detection: A Practical Guide to Classifying Political Beliefs in Text
evidence.claim: Stance is entailment relative to context C. When the target is absent, ambiguity rises (34.0 versus 19.5 percent) and accuracy depends on outside knowledge. The paper flags outside-knowledge inference as the hard step.
evidence.system_side: CU alignment = stance toward named target times target CU valence. Valence hop 0.689 versus stance hop 0.915 per the module docstring. A curated registry composed with the stance hop reached 0.782 accuracy under honest 5-fold CV on 400 tweet golds.
evidence.transfer: The paper never decomposes stance into a stance hop and a valence hop. The decomposition is the system's own design; the paper only explains why outside-knowledge steps are hard.

evidence.title: Politics of Feelings: Emotional Expression and Legislative Effectiveness in the U.S. Congress
evidence.claim: In LES models (Table 9): valence (positive minus negative emotion) +0.020 (CI 0.011 to 0.028) and intensity -0.014 (CI -0.025 to -0.004, p < 0.01). The paper reads the rise in emotion since 1973 as intensification with both positive and negative emotions rising, not as a negative turn. In the paper, intensity is the sum of the eight z-scored emotion scores.
evidence.system_side: stage5_lsd.R emits lsd_net (pos minus neg), lsd_net_norm (net divided by words) and lsd_charge ((pos plus neg) divided by words) per text. lsd_charge is a normalized dictionary-count magnitude, not a sum of classifier scores.
evidence.transfer: Supports keeping direction and intensity as separate fields rather than collapsing them. Weak transfer: floor speech vs press releases, dictionary vs transformer, and LES outcome vs CU stance or behavior. It does not show whether sign times intensity predicts behavior. Do not treat lsd_charge as the same construct as the paper's intensity; they are analogous only.
